sentences.text:
Hon'Ble Sri Justice Sambasiva Rao Naidu
 M.A.C.M.A. No.2219 Of 2016
Judgment :

The Reliance General Insurance Private Limited through its Manager filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as 'the Act') assailing the award passed by learned Chairman, Motor Accidents claims Tribunal-Cum-IX Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court at Hyderabad in O.P. No.2247 of 2013, dated 11.05.2016, wherein the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.19,05,000/- with costs of the petition and interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition.

entities.text: Motor Accidents claims Tribunal-Cum-IX Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. As could be seen from the impugned judgment it seems that the respondents 1 to 4 herein filed O.P. No.2247 of 2013 under Section 166 of the Act against the appellant and respondent No.5 and sought for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- towards compensation on account of the death of one Pulimamidi Yesu (hereinafter referred to as 'deceased') in the accident.

3. According to the petition filed before the Tribunal, it is alleged that on 12.04.2013 at about 10.00 p.m. the deceased and his friend by name Muthmar was proceeding on bike bearing No.
A.P.28.AU.5157 and when they reached the outskirts of Nadipally Village the driver of lorry bearing No. A.P.25.V.7815 which was coming from Nizamabad drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed the bike.

Therefore, the deceased and pillion rider suffered bleeding injuries and they were immediately shifted to Government Hospital, Nizamabad, on medical advice he was shifted to Gandhi Hospital, Secunderabad where he succumbed to the injuries on the next day.

4. The respondents, who are wife, children and mother of the deceased, filed the said MVOP seeking compensation against the owner of the vehicle (Respondent No.5) and appellant herein, but the owner of the lorry remained ex parte.
The appellant contested the petition, filed counter disputing the material averments.
The appellant took a specific plea that there was no negligence on the part of the lorry driver and there was contributory negligence by the deceased and sought for dismissal of the petition.
The Tribunal framed the following issues for consideration.
1. Whether the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing No.A.P.25.V.7815 caused death of Pulimamidi Yesu?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation ? If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. To what relief ?

sentences.text: During the enquiry, the wife of the deceased has been examined as P.W.1. and friend of the deceased was examined as P.W.2 and got marked Exs.A1 to Ex.A.6.
The appellant herein did not adduce any oral evidence but got marked copy of insurance policy Ex.B.1.
The Tribunal below allowed the petition in part and granted a compensation of Rs.19,05,000/-.

The appellant challenged the said award on the ground that the Court below failed to consider and appreciate the evidence of P.Ws.1 and 2 and Exs.A.1 and Ex.A.6 and came to a wrong conclusion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligence of the 5th respondent.

The appellant has claimed that since two vehicles were involved and the rider of the vehicle of the bike was negligently riding the bike, the Court below could have considered the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and could not have awarded such a huge compensation against the appellant.
6. The appellant further contended that the Court below committed an error by considering the income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month without any proof.
The deceased was an agriculturist, there was no document to believe that he was doing wood business.
Therefore, the compensation was granted by considering huge amount as monthly income of the deceased.
The appellant has claimed that the age of the deceased was wrongly considered as 38 in spite of the evidence of P.W.1 that the age of her husband was 45.
7. The appellant further contended that the Tribunal granted excess amounts under the heads of loss of estate, loss of consortium, funeral expenses, thereby sought for set aside the award.

8. Heard both parties.
9.

Now the point for consideration is :
"Whether the Tribunal failed to appreciate the evidence placed by the respondents and came to a wrong conclusion, thereby awarded excess amount as compensation,
thereby
the order is liable to be set aside"?
10. The main contention of the appellant is with regard to the alleged contributory negligence.
The appellant claims that the rider of the bike which involved in the accident was riding the bike in high speed in a negligent manner.
As already stated hereinabove, the appellant did not adduce any oral evidence in support this contention.
Even though P.W.2 was examined to prove the accident nothing could be elicited from him to establish that there was such contributory negligence by the rider of the bike.

When once the appellant took a plea that there was negligent driving of the deceased's motorcycle, without there being any evidence, the liability cannot be fixed against the rider of the motorcycle or compensation cannot be reduced.
Therefore there is no ground to consider this contention.
11. The respondents did not produce any documents in support of the alleged business of the deceased.
According to the evidence of P.W.1, her husband was an agriculturist.
They did not produce any documents to show that he has got some extents of land.

According to the description shown in the petition, the wife of the deceased was aged about 30 and eldest daughter of the deceased was aged about 18 and other son is Reliance Gen. Ins. Pvt. entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court below rightly considered the age of the deceased as 35 based on the post-mortem report and inquest report.
The appellant has claimed that P.W.1 the wife of deceased stated before the Court that her husband was 45 years old.
The wife of the deceased, who was examined as PW-1 is a household, came from village background.
She might not be aware of the actual age of her husband.
Therefore, the contention of the appellant that the Court below took a wrong figure as age of the deceased cannot be considered.
However, there is no proof about the actual income of the deceased.

In view of the absence of any evidence about the actual income of the deceased even if it is considered that the deceased was an agricultural coolie, it can be safely concluded that he can earn Rs.400/- per day, thus he can earn an amount of Rs.12,000/- per month.
To that extent the contention of the appellant herein can be considered.
There are five family members including the deceased.
Therefore, 1/5th of the said income shall be deducted towards living and personal expenses of the deceased.
As such the deceased could have contributed a sum of Rs.1,15,200/- per annum, relevant multiplier as '14'.
Therefore the financial loss on account of the death of the deceased would be Rs.16,12,800/-.
12. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the appellant, the Court below awarded excess amount towards loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses.

In the light of the observation made by the Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi1 the respondents family members of the deceased are entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/-, Rs.15,000/- and Rs.40,000/- towards loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses and thereby the same can be added.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above observation, the (2017) 16 SCC 680 respondent family members are entitled to a sum of Rs.16,82,800/-.
To that extent the award can be modified.
13. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed, compensation is reduced from Rs.19,05,000/- to Rs.16,82,800/- with costs and interest as observed by the Tribunal from the date of petition.
As a sequel, pending Miscellaneous Applications, if any, shall stand closed.
